name: Valdas Dambrauskas
headline: 8 years of struggle
lowest: At 25, he moves to London to coach. For 8 years he juggles odd jobs: newspaper delivery, gardening, pubs, never a full-time coaching post.
comeback: In 2026, after more than 20 years on the road, he leads Sabah into the Champions League, all the way to Old Trafford.
lesson: The invisible years of learning end up counting.
at25: In 2002, he wins 4,000 litas on a Lithuanian quiz show and moves to England to coach.

name: Elon Musk
headline: Days from losing everything
lowest: In 2008, SpaceX's rocket has failed three times, Tesla nears bankruptcy, and Musk's fortune is on the line as funding dries up.
comeback: In December 2008, SpaceX wins a major NASA contract and Tesla secures last-minute funding. Both companies survive.
lesson: The breaking point can come right before the turnaround.
at25: In 1996, he is CTO of Zip2, co-founded with Kimbal. Compaq buys it in 1999.

name: Nelson Mandela
headline: 27 years in prison
lowest: At 44, he is jailed for fighting apartheid. He spends over 27 years behind bars, much on Robben Island, refusing conditional release.
comeback: Released in 1990, at 71, he becomes South Africa's first democratically elected president four years later.
lesson: A life is not defined by its years of confinement.
at25: In 1944, while studying law at the University of the Witwatersrand, he co-founds the ANC Youth League.

name: Brian Chesky
headline: In debt, almost no customers
lowest: In 2008, Airbnb is not taking off. The founders pile up credit card debt and investors turn them down.
comeback: To survive, they sell cereal boxes themed on the US presidential candidates. In 2009, Airbnb joins Y Combinator and starts growing.
lesson: Survive long enough to find what works.
at25: In 2006, the RISD graduate designs toys and medical equipment in Los Angeles. Airbnb does not exist yet.

name: Patrick and John Collison
headline: 2 years for just 50 users
lowest: In 2009, the two brothers start building Stripe. For nearly 2 years, they develop payments infrastructure and negotiate with financial players.
comeback: At its September 2011 launch, Stripe has only about 50 users. It goes on to become major global payments infrastructure.
lesson: Recognizing a wrong course lets you start again.
at25: At 25, Patrick (2013) runs Stripe, valued at $1.75 billion in 2014; John (2015) is its president.

name: Leo XIV (Robert Prevost)
headline: Peru priest at 40, pope at 69
lowest: At 40, Robert Prevost trains future priests in Peru, working for many years far from the Vatican's highest offices.
comeback: He becomes a bishop at 59, a cardinal at 68, and is elected pope on May 8, 2025, at 69.
lesson: A long life in the field can lead to the top.
at25: In 1981, the Augustinian friar studies theology in Chicago and takes solemn vows, a year before ordination.

name: José Hernández
headline: Rejected 11 times by NASA
lowest: The son of Mexican migrant farmworkers, he works California's fields. Once an engineer, he is turned down by NASA eleven times.
comeback: In May 2004, on his twelfth try, NASA selects him. On August 28, 2009, he flies aboard Discovery to the International Space Station.
lesson: Eleven rejections do not decide the twelfth.
at25: In 1987, he joins Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory as an electrical engineer. NASA selects him only in 2004.

name: Margaret Thatcher
headline: Grocer's daughter, Prime Minister
lowest: She grows up above the family grocery in Grantham. After studying chemistry, she loses the 1950 and 1951 elections.
comeback: Elected an MP in 1959, she becomes the UK's first woman Prime Minister in 1979, at 53, and governs over 11 years.
lesson: Record unpopularity does not necessarily end a career.
image_credit: Margaret Thatcher Foundation (recadrage : Begoon), Libre de droits (Copyrighted free use)
at25: In 1950 and 1951, Margaret Roberts works as a chemist and runs for Parliament in Dartford, losing twice.

name: Jensen Huang
headline: Close to running out of cash
lowest: Nvidia's first chip, the NV1 (1995), flops and Sega drops it. Nearly out of cash, Huang lays off over half the staff in 1996.
comeback: In 1997, with a month of payroll left, the RIVA 128 sells about a million units in four months. Nvidia later leads AI computing.
lesson: Admitting a mistake can save the project.
at25: In 1988, he is an LSI Logic engineer, studying at night at Stanford. He co-founds Nvidia in 1993.

name: Robert Downey Jr.
headline: From prison to Iron Man
lowest: Arrested in 1996 with drugs and a gun, he keeps relapsing: three years in prison in 1999, fired from Ally McBeal in 2001.
comeback: Sober, he plays Tony Stark in Iron Man (2008), relaunching his career. In 2024, he wins an Oscar for Oppenheimer.
at25: In 1990, he co-stars with Mel Gibson in Air America. Chaplin earns him an Oscar nomination in 1992.

name: Walt Disney
headline: Bankrupt at 21, then built Disney
lowest: In 1923, at 21, his Kansas City studio Laugh-O-Gram goes bankrupt. In 1928, he loses Oswald the Lucky Rabbit to Universal, with most animators.
comeback: In 1923, he and his brother Roy start the Disney company. Mickey Mouse arrives in 1928, Snow White in 1937, Disneyland in 1955.
image_credit: Boy Scouts of America, Public domain
at25: In 1927, he and Ub Iwerks create Oswald the Lucky Rabbit for Universal at his Los Angeles studio.

name: Henry Ford
headline: Two failed car companies before Ford
lowest: His Detroit Automobile Company, founded in 1899, folds in 1901; in 1902 he leaves the Henry Ford Company, which becomes Cadillac.
comeback: He founds Ford Motor Company on June 16, 1903. The Model T arrives in 1908, then the moving assembly line in 1913.
lesson: A failed start is not the end.
at25: Married to Clara Bryant in April 1888, he runs a lumber business on his father's former farmland.
